newsitem.title: USA: NAPM sees moderate manufacturing growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: NAPM sees moderate manufacturing growth in 1997.

text.p: The economy is looking up, the nation's manufacturers said Tuesday in an early glimpse of 1997, saying they expect moderate growth with slightly lower material costs but expect to pay slightly more for labour.

The National Association of Purchasing Management, in its semiannual forecast, said it expects a 5.4 percent revenue growth on average in 1997, with a 0.5 percent drop in prices paid for materials in the first four months of next year.
For 1996, the group reported a 4.9 percent gain in overall revenues, down from a 7.4 percent increase reported in 1995.
The report from the Tempe, Ariz.-based group also predicted overall prices to remain unchanged in 1997, while labour and benefit costs will increase by 2.8 percent.
NAMP is comprised of purchasing and supply management executives at manufacturing companies across the nation. Its surveys are closely watched as gauges of future economic activity.

NAPM Business Survey Committee Chairman Ralph Kauffman said members are more optimistic now than they were a year ago, "with 80 percent of them expecting business in the first half of 1997 to be better than or the same as the second half of 1996."
NAPM executives predicted capital expenditures will fall 1.6 percent in 1997. In addition, survey respondents indicated production capacity will increase 5.8 percent in 1997.

NAPM members say they expect stronger holiday retail sales in 1996 compared with 1995, but not as strong as in 1994. Of the respondents, 55 percent saw average holiday sales, while 44 percent forecast "good holiday sales."

NAPM members see the dollar rising against the mark and yen in 1997, with 50 percent saying the dollar will stronger versus the yen and 45 percent saying the dollar will be stronger against the mark. Only 27 percent saw the dollar weakening against the yen, and 22 percent weakening against the mark in 1997.
Separately, Kauffman said he will leave his post on Jan. 2, 1997. He will be succeeded by Norbert Ore, who is currently a purchasing director for SONOCO Products Co.
